senate.title: Eliminate the legislative filibuster
senate.what: Changes Senate rules so most bills can pass with a simple majority instead of 60 votes, which would let a Democratic majority move much of this agenda without Republican support.

senate.title: Re-elect Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader
senate.what: Decides whether Chuck Schumer stays as leader of the Senate Democratic caucus, which shapes who sets the floor schedule and the party's strategy for the next two years.

senate.title: Medicare for All Act
senate.what: Replaces private insurance with a single public plan covering every American, ending premiums and deductibles but requiring large new federal taxes to pay for it.

senate.title: Restore the enhanced ACA premium tax credits
senate.what: Brings back the larger ACA marketplace subsidies that expired after 2025, lowering premiums for millions of people who buy their own coverage.

senate.title: Repeal the OBBBA Medicaid cuts and work requirements
senate.what: Reverses the Medicaid funding cuts and new work requirements in the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, keeping coverage for people projected to lose it.

senate.title: Lower drug prices: expand Medicare negotiation, cap insulin costs, rein in PBMs
senate.what: Lowers drug prices by letting Medicare negotiate many more drugs, capping insulin costs for everyone, and reining in the pharmacy benefit managers who set what patients pay.

senate.title: Curb prior authorization (Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act)
senate.what: Requires Medicare Advantage plans to approve routine care faster through electronic prior authorization, cutting delays for patients and paperwork for doctors.

senate.title: Create a public health insurance option or Medicare buy-in
senate.what: Lets people buy into a government-run health plan or Medicare alongside private insurance, adding a lower-cost choice without ending private coverage.

senate.title: Protect and expand Social Security and Medicare: no benefit cuts, and the wealthy pay in (lift the payroll-tax cap)
senate.what: Rules out cuts to Social Security and Medicare benefits and has high earners pay more into them, usually by lifting the cap on wages subject to the payroll tax, to keep both funded for decades.

senate.title: Protect rural hospitals: more funding, and undo the hit from the Medicaid cuts
senate.what: Sends more money to rural hospitals and undoes the hit they take from the 2025 Medicaid cuts, aimed at keeping emergency rooms and maternity wards from closing.

senate.title: Expand mental health care: parity enforcement, crisis lines and school counselors
senate.what: Expands mental health care through stronger insurance parity enforcement, more money for the 988 crisis line and more school counselors.

senate.title: Codify Roe: the Women's Health Protection Act
senate.what: Creates a federal right to provide and receive abortion care, overriding most state bans and restrictions passed since Roe v. Wade was overturned.

senate.title: Right to IVF Act
senate.what: Creates a federal right to IVF and other fertility treatment and requires many insurers to cover it, protecting access after state court rulings put clinics at risk.

senate.title: Make data centers pay their own power costs and cap utility hikes
senate.what: Requires data centers to cover the full cost of the power and grid upgrades they need and limits utility rate increases, so households aren't left paying for the AI boom.

senate.title: Lower energy bills: restore the clean-energy tax credits the OBBBA cut (Lowering Electric Bills Act)
senate.what: Restores the clean-energy tax credits for solar, wind, batteries, home upgrades and EVs that the 2025 OBBBA cut, which backers say would lower power bills by adding cheap generation.

senate.title: Expand the Child Tax Credit
senate.what: Makes the Child Tax Credit larger and available in full to low-income families, which cut child poverty sharply when it was temporarily expanded in 2021.

senate.title: A middle-class income tax cut (Keep Your Pay Act / Working Americans' Tax Cut Act)
senate.what: Cuts federal income taxes for middle-class families, for example by exempting the first $75,000 of a couple's income, paid for by taxes on the wealthy.

senate.title: Lower child care costs: cap at 7% of income, universal child care, or bigger subsidies
senate.what: Cuts child care costs, for example by capping them at 7% of family income or funding universal child care, so working parents pay far less.

senate.title: Reverse the OBBBA's SNAP (food assistance) cuts
senate.what: Reverses the 2025 OBBBA cuts to SNAP food assistance, including its new work rules and the cost shift to states, restoring benefits for millions of people.

senate.title: Repeal the OBBBA top-bracket cuts and close billionaire loopholes
senate.what: Undoes the 2025 tax cuts for the highest earners and closes loopholes used by billionaires, raising revenue for other priorities.

senate.title: National paid family and medical leave
senate.what: Guarantees workers paid time off to care for a new child, a sick relative or their own illness, funded through a national insurance program.

senate.title: Raise the minimum wage ($15–$25) and expand overtime
senate.what: Raises the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to between $15 and $25 an hour and expands overtime pay, giving raises to millions of low-wage workers.

senate.title: PRO Act and union rights
senate.what: Makes it easier to form a union and harder for employers to block one, with penalties for illegal firings during organizing drives.

senate.title: Ban congressional stock trading: the Peters–Hawley–Merkley–Ossoff bill, covering the President and VP
senate.what: Bars members of Congress, the President and the Vice President from trading individual stocks while in office, removing a major conflict of interest.

senate.title: Pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act
senate.what: Restores the Voting Rights Act's preclearance system, so states and localities with recent voting discrimination need federal approval before changing election rules.

senate.title: Ban partisan gerrymandering
senate.what: Bans partisan gerrymandering of congressional districts nationwide, so maps can't be drawn to lock in one party's advantage.

senate.title: DC and Puerto Rico statehood
senate.what: Admits Washington, DC and Puerto Rico as states, giving their residents full voting representation in Congress and adding four senators.

senate.title: Get big money out: ban corporate PACs and super PACs, overturn Citizens United
senate.what: Gets big money out of elections by banning corporate PACs and super PACs and amending the Constitution to overturn Citizens United.

senate.title: Pass the Equality Act (LGBTQ civil rights)
senate.what: Adds sexual orientation and gender identity to federal civil-rights law, banning anti-LGBTQ discrimination in jobs, housing, public places and federal programs.

senate.title: Universal background checks (Background Check Expansion Act)
senate.what: Requires a background check on nearly every gun sale, including private and online sales that skip checks today.

senate.title: Comprehensive immigration reform
senate.what: Overhauls the immigration system by pairing border security with a path to legal status for long-time undocumented residents.

senate.title: Rein in or abolish ICE: no masks, body cameras, visible ID, judicial warrants, right to sue
senate.what: Puts limits on ICE, such as no masks, body cameras and visible ID, judicial warrants and a right to sue, or replaces the agency altogether.

senate.title: Condition military aid to Israel
senate.what: Puts conditions on U.S. military aid to Israel, such as limits on offensive weapons, tied to how the weapons are used in Gaza.

senate.title: Iran War Powers Resolution
senate.what: Uses the War Powers Resolution to require congressional approval for continued U.S. military action against Iran.

senate.title: End the tariff emergencies and pass the Trade Review Act
senate.what: Ends the emergency declarations behind the current tariffs and requires Congress to approve new ones, which would lower import costs for businesses and shoppers.

senate.title: AI guardrails
senate.what: Sets federal safety and accountability rules for AI and keeps states free to pass their own protections.

governor.title: Expand Medicaid and raise provider rates
governor.what: Extends Medicaid to low-income adults in states that haven't expanded and raises payments to providers, adding coverage and helping rural hospitals stay open.

governor.title: Lower drug prices: a state price board, PBM limits, insulin caps
governor.what: Lowers drug prices with a state board that can cap what is paid for costly drugs, limits on pharmacy benefit managers, and insulin caps.

governor.title: A state public option or universal coverage
governor.what: Creates a state-backed public health plan or a path to universal coverage, giving people a lower-cost option.

governor.title: Cancel medical debt and keep it off credit reports
governor.what: Buys up and erases residents' medical debt and bars it from credit reports, so illness doesn't wreck people's ability to rent or borrow.

governor.title: End prior authorization and insulin co-pays
governor.what: Ends insurer pre-approval rules for routine care and caps or eliminates insulin co-pays, speeding treatment and cutting out-of-pocket costs.

governor.title: Expand mental health care: crisis lines, school counselors, parity
governor.what: Expands mental health care with crisis lines and mobile teams, more school counselors and tougher enforcement of insurance parity.

governor.title: Protect rural hospitals: state funding, Medicaid rates, rural health plans
governor.what: Keeps rural hospitals open with state money, higher Medicaid rates and rural health plans.

governor.title: Make data centers pay their full costs, or pause them until they do
governor.what: Makes data centers pay the full cost of the power and grid upgrades they need, or pauses new ones until rules are in place, so households don't foot the bill.

governor.title: Utility bills: accountability, caps on fees, rate freezes and price caps
governor.what: Holds utilities accountable with caps on fees and limits on their political influence, and freezes rates or caps power prices when bills spike.

governor.title: Clean energy to lower bills: clean-power standards, buildout, home-energy rebates
governor.what: Builds more clean power and adopts clean-electricity standards and home-energy rebates, which backers say will cut power bills over time.

governor.title: Build more homes: ease zoning, speed permits, add supply
governor.what: Builds more homes by easing zoning, speeding permits and adding supply, often with statewide rules that override local limits.

governor.title: Down payment help and a broker-fee ban
governor.what: Gives first-time buyers help with down payments and bans renters from paying brokers' fees, lowering the upfront cost of a home or apartment.

governor.title: Renter protections and limits on corporate landlords
governor.what: Protects renters with limits on junk fees, algorithmic rent-setting and no-cause evictions, and reins in corporate landlords buying up homes.

governor.title: Targeted property-tax relief
governor.what: Cuts property taxes for homeowners, often targeted to seniors and middle-income families, sometimes paid for by ending corporate breaks.

governor.title: Middle-class tax cuts
governor.what: Cuts state income taxes for middle-class families, for example through a bigger standard deduction or no tax on tips and overtime.

governor.title: A millionaire's tax
governor.what: Adds a higher income tax rate on earnings above $1 million, raising revenue for housing, schools or other priorities.

governor.title: $15 minimum wage
governor.what: Raises the state minimum wage to $15 an hour, giving raises to the lowest-paid workers.

governor.title: Workforce training and apprenticeships
governor.what: Expands apprenticeships and free job training so workers can move into better-paying jobs.

governor.title: Fully fund public schools: raise K-12 funding or fix the formula
governor.what: Raises state K-12 funding or rewrites the school funding formula so districts, especially poor and rural ones, get enough to pay teachers and run schools.

governor.title: Universal pre-K
governor.what: Offers free pre-K to every four-year-old (and sometimes three-year-olds), helping kids start school ready and saving parents child care costs.

governor.title: Lower child care costs: universal child care or bigger subsidies
governor.what: Lowers child care costs through universal child care or much larger state subsidies for working families.

governor.title: Raise teacher pay
governor.what: Raises teacher pay, such as a higher minimum starting salary, to recruit and keep teachers.

governor.title: Fund public schools fully instead of vouchers
governor.what: Opposes or repeals private-school voucher programs and puts that money into fully funding public schools.

governor.title: Lower college costs: free community college, tuition-free public college
governor.what: Makes community college free, or public college tuition-free, for recent graduates and working adults.

governor.title: AI safeguards and online protections for kids
governor.what: Sets state rules for AI and protects kids online, such as limits on addictive social media feeds and AI chatbots aimed at minors.

governor.title: Paid family and medical leave
governor.what: Creates a state insurance program that gives workers paid time off for a new child, a sick relative or their own illness.

governor.title: Fund public safety and violence prevention
governor.what: Pays for more police and for community violence-intervention programs, aimed at lowering violent crime.

governor.title: Gun safety laws: universal background checks, red-flag laws
governor.what: Passes gun safety laws such as universal background checks and red-flag laws that let courts take guns from people judged dangerous.

governor.title: Write abortion rights into state law
governor.what: Writes the right to abortion into state law or the state constitution, protecting access regardless of federal action.

governor.title: Limit ICE cooperation, including barring ICE from schools and other sensitive places
governor.what: Limits state and local help to ICE and bars immigration arrests at schools, hospitals, courthouses and churches without a judge's warrant.

governor.title: Keep a federalized National Guard out of the state without the governor's consent
governor.what: Opposes a president federalizing the National Guard, or sending in another state's troops, over the governor's objection, through lawsuits, refusals and state laws. State laws can bar other states' troops sent under Title 32, but not a president's Title 10 federalization, which only courts have checked.

governor.title: Fight Trump's tariffs: sue, push back, relief for hit businesses and farmers
governor.what: Fights Trump's tariffs by suing over them, pushing back publicly and helping businesses and farmers hit by higher costs.

governor.title: National Popular Vote Interstate Compact
governor.what: Joins the interstate compact to award the state's electoral votes to the national popular-vote winner, which takes effect once states with 270 votes sign on.

governor.title: Voting access: automatic voter registration and a state voting rights act
governor.what: Registers eligible voters automatically and passes a state voting rights act protecting access to the ballot.

governor.title: Anti-fraud overhaul (audits, inspector general)
governor.what: Overhauls oversight of state programs with surprise audits and an independent inspector general to catch fraud and waste.
